stories.title: Chinese rescue workers search for 558 missing after Nepal-Tibet floods
stories.summary: A mudslide on the China-Nepal border killed three people and left 558 missing, including 260 foreign nationals. Over 1,000 rescuers with dogs, drones, and boats are searching despite difficult terrain and an unstable reservoir upstream. Relief supplies arrive by air while risks of further landslides remain high due to ongoing rainfall. Three people died and 558 others were still missing after a mudslide in Tibet on the China-Nepal border, Chinese state media reported on Aug 27, citing local officials. Of the missing, 260 were foreign nationals, it said. More than a thousand rescuers, equipped with dogs and drones, were searching for survivors after a wall of mud and debris swept over buildings on the Chinese side of the border on the morning of Aug 26. A clip of surveillance video from the Chinese side of the frontier showed dozens of people running for their lives as the surge crashed down. Rescue operations face multiple challenges, including “the instability of a reservoir lake upstream” and “the narrow mountain road”, Li Qipu, a member of China’s paramilitary People’s Armed. Police, told state broadcaster CCTV. Large vehicles and heavy equipment cannot currently reach the main disaster zone, although surrounding roads remain open, allowing supplies to get in from behind, according to the broadcaster. Authorities have dispatched nearly 800 people and more than 150 vehicles to the border area, according to state news agency Xinhua. The fire service has deployed 431 personnel, working with search dogs, life-detection scanners, and small boats, it said.

stories.title: Number of people missing after China landslide reaches 558
stories.summary: BEIJING, August 27. At least 558 people are missing following a landslide at China’s Gyirong border crossing on the border with Nepal, China Central Television reported. According to the broadcaster, 260 of the 558 people missing are foreign nationals. As Xinhua reported, the landslide occurred at the Gyirong border crossing at around 10:30 a.m. on August 26 on the Nepalese side of the border. Three people were killed.

stories.title: Japan fast-tracks anti-drone system amid China’s military build-up
stories.summary: Tokyo is experimenting with a radically faster way of buying new weapons – picking a domestically built interceptor drone less than three months after launching the procurement process. Analysts say this shift could help Japan respond more quickly to China’s expanding military capabilities. The defence ministry’s Acquisition, Technology and Logistics Agency (ATLA) announced on Tuesday that it had signed a contract to buy Terra Drone’s Terra B1 system following competitive trials. stories.title: Creating a second home for residents of Hong Kong’s subdivided flats
stories.summary: A proper kitchen, a washing machine and a table where children can do their homework – these are some of the bare necessities that people expect for their homes. But for many families living in subdivided flats in Hong Kong, that is unfortunately not the reality.
